sermon.title: The King’s Servants
sermon.speaker: Guest speaker (name not given in the recording)
sermon.summary: In this message a guest speaker at Vine Cluster Church reads Esther 3–7 as a parable of the new covenant. He says Haman pictures the proud scribes and Pharisees and Mordecai pictures Jesus, who would not bow to them. He then follows Esther going before the king, her two banquets, and Haman’s end, and closes by urging believers to surrender old ways.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. The speaker is a guest, not Pastor Kincer, and continues the Esther study from “Revelations of the King’s Wife” (“two weeks ago”); the recording does not give his name. Editor notes: the captions garble a few phrases, shown as [unclear] (“king [unclear] walk around,” “[unclear] Haman,” “royal [unclear],” “come to [unclear] with herself,” “two [unclear]”); “cat-o’-nine-tails,” “rent in two” and the verse numbers “Esther 5:2” and “4:11” are caption corrections. He cites “Matthew 20 verse 34” and “Mark 6 34” for Jesus’ compassion (correct), reads Matthew 26:59-style words about false witnesses without naming the chapter, and says “Matthew’s like 29 chapters 26 20 I don’t know” (Matthew has 28 chapters). His statements about the dates of the Lord’s Supper and the Passover, and that “they still believe that the messiah hasn’t come yet,” are his own and are not verified here. He also mentions real people by first name in passing and makes a joke about celebrities; these appear in the transcript only. His comparisons of Haman to the scribes and Pharisees and of Esther’s story to the New Testament are his own interpretation.

faqs.question: Does he say Mordecai worked for the king?
faqs.answer: No. He says “mordecai wasn’t necessarily employed by the king,” and that although he had always pictured him as a servant of the king, he went looking for where it says so and “it’s not there.”

faqs.question: What does he say about Haman’s pride?
faqs.answer: He says Haman “loved the attention and the praise,” everyone was to bow, and he was so upset when Mordecai did not bow. He says Haman “was all about himself” and was “so prideful.”

faqs.question: What does he mean by the new covenant and “the new Israel”?
faqs.answer: He says Esther was “the example of new the new Israel,” so “no longer is it only the nation of Israel it’s anyone who pleases the king,” and he thanks God “we’re part of the new covenant.”

faqs.question: What does he say happened when Jesus was twelve?
faqs.answer: He says Jesus’ parents thought he was with them, went back to the temple and found him “asking questions” and talking with the priests. He says Jesus said “I’m supposed to be about my father’s business,” which was “to complete the new covenant.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: And He said to them, “Why did you seek Me? Did you not know that I must be about My Father’s business?”

faqs.question: What law did Haman get the king to pass?
faqs.answer: He says Haman “bribed the king” and was “willing to pay ten thousand talents of silver to get rid of all the Jews,” and that “the scribes wrote and sealed the law to destroy them.” He says “this is an actual historical event.”

faqs.question: What does he say about a Christian who feels like he is just following rules?
faqs.answer: He says “you don’t want to get stuck in that mindset that God is just a bunch of rules,” and that it should be a desire “to please him” as when you first met your wife and ask “how can I make you happy.”

faqs.question: What does the golden scepter mean in his message?
faqs.answer: He says it “meant that she was accepted,” and since “she’s the new covenant” and “the new church,” we can “go in to the inner court where the king is” and “speak to the king yourself.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: So it was, when the king saw Queen Esther standing in the court, that she found favor in his sight, and the king held out to Esther the golden scepter that was in his hand. Then Esther went near and touched the top of the scepter.

faqs.question: What does he say about Jesus and the Passover?
faqs.answer: He says “Jesus Christ was killed on the 14th day of the first month the same day as the Passover,” and that “Jesus Christ is the Passover lamb.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: On the fourteenth day of the first month at twilight is the LORD’s Passover.

faqs.question: What does he say the scribes and Pharisees believed about the Messiah?
faqs.answer: He says “they didn’t realize that they were killing the son of God” and that they “still believe that the messiah hasn’t come yet.” He then warns “we don’t want to be that way church.”

faqs.question: What does he say about being an example to others?
faqs.answer: He says “we do not want to be Christians that where people cannot follow our example,” and asks “how are my actions influencing the people around me.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Therefore whatever they tell you to observe, that observe and do, but do not do according to their works; for they say, and do not do.

faqs.question: What does he say stopped when Jesus died?
faqs.answer: He says “the old covenant the old way stopped,” including “the burnt offerings” and “the ceremonies,” and that “everyone now can come in” and “has an opportunity.”

faqs.question: What does he say the scribes and Pharisees loved about the temple?
faqs.answer: He says they loved “to look at it and go into it and everybody see them go into the temple,” while Jesus “never wanted to dwell with temples made with hands” and “always wanted to dwell in our hearts.”
